articles.title: Ross County have 102 goals and British football’s best start but is it a fairytale?
articles.summary: There is cynicism and jealousy but one of County’s top scorers is 39 as club try to climb leagues again after tumbling. It was a vidiprinter moment worthy of a double take. Ross County 1 Cove Rangers 1 (Keir 52).
body: Assessment from the captain, Brian Graham, of a frankly irrelevant loss on penalties to Stenhousemuir in the Challenge Cup epitomises the County approach. “We should have been five- or six-nil up at half-time,” an irked Graham says. “That shows the standards we have set. We lost a dubious goal, which shouldn’t have stood.” Earlier in that competition County whacked 14 past a Hearts youth side before defeating a Celtic B team including two Chelsea loanees and a £3m midfielder.

Unsurprisingly there is cynicism, laced with jealousy, about County’s position. They are portrayed as wild spenders in a frugal environment. A club in the wrong competitive domain. The analysis does not stack up. Graham, the scorer of 21 goals across all competitions, is 39. The prominent Adam Emslie was last on loan at Cove after being rejected by Aberdeen. Luke McCarvel arrived via Kelty Hearts and Cumbernauld Colts. Lewis Reid is previously of Stranraer, Lewis Strapp a signing from Airdrie. County have a batch of Scottish Championship-capable players, not Premiership-ready ones. Their form is still extraordinary.

articles.title: Russell: Hamilton ruthless like Verstappen but has grace and values
articles.summary: George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally "ruthless competitor" to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has "incredible values, grace and dignity".
body: Russell and Verstappen's rivalry reignited last weekend at the Las Vegas Grand Prix following a minor collision between the pair in practice, after which the Mercedes driver publicly criticised his Red Bull rival's conduct.

Verstappen won a thrilling race in Las Vegas that saw Russell challenge him for the lead for long periods before crashing and finishing ninth, and afterwards the four-time world champion said the Brit is "so far below my level" before adding that it was "fantastic" seeing him make an error.

Speaking exclusively to Martin Brundle during an interview that will air during Sky Sports F1's live coverage of the Qatar Grand Prix on Sunday, Russell said he found Verstappen's verbal attack on him "amusing", before drawing a comparison between the Dutchman and seven-time world champion Hamilton.
"He [Verstappen] is a ruthless competitor and I massively respect that, but there's also Lewis Hamilton, who I've spent three years team-mates with and watched my whole life," Russell said.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin calls Steelers ‘dumpster fire’ as Brady rips Rodgers for breaking locker room sanctity
articles.summary: Ex-coach says QB was ‘beloved’ by teammates. Rodgers released after diatribe about McCarthy. Mike Tomlin, who coached Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers last year, and Tom Brady, one of Rodgers’s longtime peers as an elite quarterback, ⁠weighed in Thursday on Rodgers’s dramatic exit from Pittsburgh…
body: “I’m upset about it,” Tomlin said at half-time of NBC’s Thanksgiving night broadcast of the Kansas City Chiefs-Buffalo Bills game. “It’s a dumpster fire, and I don’t say that in a judgmental way. I’ve presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years, but it certainly is upsetting and I’m sure Steeler Nation is upset.”

The Steelers announced Tuesday night that Rodgers would be benched in favor of Mason Rudolph. The ⁠next day, Rodgers went ⁠on the Pat McAfee ​Show and said, “I’m not going back to Pittsburgh” while making unflattering behind-the-scenes allegations about Steelers coach Mike McCarthy.

According to Rodgers, McCarthy was “snoring” after ⁠arriving late to a quarterbacks meeting on 18 November and missed meetings and walkthroughs during the remainder of the week. During half-time of Pittsburgh’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on ⁠Sunday, McCarthy broke a huddle of offensive players with “1, 2, 3 Packers,” Rodgers revealed – a fact later ​confirmed by McCarthy.

The Steelers waived Rodgers later on Wednesday, ‌and he became a free ‌agent on Thursday when he cleared waivers. Team owner Art Rooney II has backed McCarthy and described Rodgers’s actions as “insubordination”.

“It’s a dumpster fire, and I don’t say that in a judgmental way.

articles.title: Fury cleared to fight Joshua after medical checks
articles.summary: Tyson Fury is medically cleared to fight Anthony Joshua in December after the bout was put in jeopardy by claims of a schizophrenia diagnosis.
body: Fury, 38, spoke of his mental health struggles in a Netflix documentary which was released on Friday, with his wife, Paris, saying he had been diagnosed with schizophrenia.
But Paris has since retracted that statement, saying he "doesn't have this condition" and Netflix have edited the remarks out of their film.
The British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC) told BBC Sport: "Tyson Fury has been cleared to box on 11 December."
Fury faces Joshua, 37, in a long overdue all-British heavyweight contest at Cardiff's Principality Stadium in the early hours of 12 December.

articles.title: Overton rips through Australia as England storm to 2-1 series lead
articles.summary: Jamie Overton claimed career-best T20I figures of 5-12 and was involved in seven wickets in total as England hammered Australia by seven wickets on DLS in Brisbane to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match T20 international series.
body: Seam-bowling all-rounder Overton had bagged eye-watering figures of 1-44 from three overs and 1-28 from two across England's defeat in Melbourne at the weekend and victory in Carrara on Tuesday, going at an economy rate of 14.

But he ripped through Australia at The Gabba as the hosts flapped against his cross-seamers and bounce, ending a game-altering spell with a double-wicket-maiden in the 13th over to help roll Mitch Marsh's men for 108, their lowest T20 score at home, in 16.5 overs.

A successful chase appeared a formality at halfway but a stumble to 49-3 around three rain delays, as Harry Brook (9) and Aneurin Donald (32 off 12) followed Phil Salt (5) in being dismissed by Riley Meredith (3-30), gave Australia a sliver of hope before Jordan Cox (33no off 14) - dropped on one by Nikhil Chaudhary - took England to a revised 93 in 8.5 overs, well inside the new 16-over limit.

Donald backed up his 85 from 32 balls on the Gold Coast three nights ago, with his six boundaries in Brisbane (five fours and a six) including three in a row off towering seamer Billy Stanlake, who was making his first T20 international appearance since 2019.

articles.title: England outclass Aussies again to take series lead
articles.summary: England reaffirm their advantage over a struggling Australia in white-ball cricket with a seven-wicket thrashing in the third T20 at The Gabba.
body: Fresh from their eight-wicket win on Tuesday, England bowled Australia out for 108 - the lowest total the hosts have been dismissed for in a T20 at home.
Jamie Overton had struggled to this point on the tour but claimed his first international five-wicket haul in taking a remarkable 5-12. Spinner Liam Dawson also chipped in again with 3-16.
From there, despite England slipping to 49-3, the most likely route to Australia escaping without defeat appeared to be the weather in Brisbane.
After three rain delays, Harry Brook's side reached their revised target of 93 with 7.1 overs to spare, claiming victory via the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method.

articles.title: Brighton's perfect blend: The duo key to Seagulls' rise
articles.summary: It was a painful Sunday afternoon at Hull, but by the time Brighton pair Luka Vuskovic and Pascal Gross arrived at the beachside restaurant on Tuesday, you got the impression they didn't need too much of the bracing near-frozen sea air to boost the mood.
body: Yes, they were disappointed, but they weren't going to let a few minutes and Oli McBurnie overshadow a start to the season that has taken the Seagulls second in the Premier League table after 11 games.

Not many would have predicted such a lofty position for Fabian Hurzeler's team - including some of the Brighton team themselves - but the club are playing some thrilling football, and the 26 goals they have scored has helped them beat the likes of Arsenal and Man City already this season.

Sitting in front of me are two of the reasons why. They are both too modest to entertain that, but at the heart of this side's success is an almost seamless tactical and generational blend epitomised by Gross and Vuskovic.
Gross has been a revelation since his return earlier this year, something he admits he was nervous about doing. "You always hope for the best, but you never know. Coming back is not always easy."

articles.title: Magnus Bradbury makes first Scotland start in a year against Argentina
articles.summary: Back-rower Magnus Bradbury will make his first start in a year for injury-hit Scotland in their Nations Championship finals weekend clash with Argentina at Allianz Stadium on Sunday.
body: Head coach Gregor Townsend is unable to call on a string of senior players, including captain Sione Tuipulotu, Ben White, Pierre Schoeman, Scott Cummings, and back-row trio Matt Fagerson, Jack Dempsey and Jamie Ritchie.

The absence of Fagerson and Dempsey has paved the way for Edinburgh forward Bradbury, who was not named in the initial squad for this month’s matches, to start in the number eight jersey for the first time since the victory over Tonga last November.
The situation in the back-row has been improved by the fact flanker Rory Darge is fit enough to return and captain the side after a shoulder issue forced him to miss last weekend’s win over Japan.

After Townsend rotated his side heavily for that match, Blair Kinghorn, Kyle Steyn, Huw Jones and Finn Russell return to join Darcy Graham, Rory Hutchinson and Jamie Dobie in a more familiar-looking backline.
